A1.justification: Both complete, readable 23-page PDFs describe L4Q. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original CSQA/MMLU accuracy, memory, training-time and throughput measurements, plus initialization, warm-up, and rank ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains original accuracy and efficiency measurements and adds Mistral results, group-size experiments, and a training-convergence comparison.

M1.justification: The core quantization, weight merging, gradient reuse, and initialization equations are retained. However, v4 explicitly prescribes LoRA-only warm-up in Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1, whereas v5 omits this specification without explaining whether the procedure changed. An actual removal of warm-up from training cannot be established.

E1.justification: Both use Stanford-Alpaca training data and the same seven commonsense tasks and MMLU evaluations. Adding Mistral changes the evaluated model configuration, not the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: v5 adds LSQ/QAT to the training-time comparison in Table 11; v4 Table 9 compared only QLoRA*, QA-LoRA, and L4Q. The accuracy comparator set is retained. The complete memory comparison moves to v5 Table 10, with QAT identified as LSQ, rather than losing comparators.

E3.justification: v5 adds Mistral-v0.1 7B with rank 8, replaces LLaMA-1 7B with LLaMA-2 7B in the rank ablation, and introduces group sizes 32/64/128 and a convergence comparison using a shared learning rate of 2e-5. New LSQ timing measurements use two/four A100 GPUs for 13B/33B. Existing data splits and 50K/25K training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplementary analysis changes substantially: v4's warm-up study and Table 5 disappear; the rank study is replaced with LLaMA-2 results; and v5 adds quantization-group sensitivity in Appendix C.2 and controlled convergence curves in Figure 5. The initialization analysis remains, including Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across runs. Quantization and clipping errors measure approximation error, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantial Mistral and group-size results, replaces rank-ablation results, removes warm-up results, and adds convergence findings and LSQ timings. For example, new 4-bit Mistral L4Q scores are 66.1% CSQA and 61.4% MMLU 5-shot. The 33B training times change from 36.2 to 39.6 hours for QA-LoRA and 39.6 to 37.9 for L4Q, reversing their ordering. Retained OpenLLaMA/LLaMA benchmark, initialization-table, memory, and throughput values match.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, STE-based gradient derivations, and initialization formulas remain mathematically equivalent, including Appendices A and B. Equations are split, renumbered, and reworded; the initialization condition b = 0 remains in Appendix B.

C1.justification: Both versions claim joint quantization and low-rank adaptation, fully quantized inference, memory-efficient training, and improved low-bit accuracy. The later abstract's Mistral mention and explicit 4-bit/3-bit wording summarize expanded evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v5 adds specific untested extensions involving activation quantization, KV-cache compression, and LoRA initialization. Appendix D attributes the retained shorter training budget to faster convergence and reduced overfitting; Appendix E explains per-step recomputation costs and the potential use of paged optimizers. The earlier warm-up interpretation and associated failure conditions disappear.

D1.justification: v5 fills previously unspecified QA-LoRA learning rates for LLaMA-2 with 2e-5 and documents Mistral settings and multi-GPU LSQ timing. It removes Algorithm 1's initialization/warm-up details and the reproducibility statement pointing to supplementary source code. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish that code availability itself changed.

R1.justification: v5 adds Jiang et al. (2023) for Mistral and Qin et al. (2024), positioning the latter alongside QLoRA-derived methods with mixed-precision inference limitations. Section 2.4 also explicitly acknowledges QA-LoRA's shared objective. The remaining positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: v5 substantially condenses and rewrites the abstract, quantization background, gradient explanations, initialization discussion, and experimental narrative. It removes Section 3.4 and the reproducibility statement, adds a limitations section, and reorganizes the appendices around hyperparameters and training efficiency.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, Figure 1 moves to the opening page, Figure 3 shrinks from five panels to three, and Figure 5 is added. The memory comparison is divided between a shortened main table and the full appendix table; detailed benchmark tables are split across Tables 13a/b and 14a/b. Figures 1, 2, and 4 retain identical graphics.

improvement.justification: Mistral validation, group-size sensitivity, and the controlled convergence comparison strengthen empirical support and practical guidance. The added limitations and efficiency discussion also clarify scope and costs. These gains are tempered by removing the warm-up study and algorithm documentation, which weakens procedural transparency. Overall, the added evidence supports a limited net improvement.
